newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Northwest Airlines aids China flood victims.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Airlines aids China flood victims.

text.p: Northwest Airlines is donating the use of one of its Boeing 747 freighters to help the victims of flooding in China, a Northwest statement said on Thursday.

The airline said it was teaming up with the private disaster relief agency AmeriCares to send 175,000 pounds of humanitarian relief supplies to approximately six million Chinese citizens left homeless as a result of catastrophic flooding along the Yangtze River.
Medicines, hospital and surgical equipment, shelter material and food, including thousands of pounds of soup, have already been transported from several U.S. cities to Tokyo.
The 85 tonnes of supplies are due to be flown to Shanghai on September 9, the statement said.
The aid will be given to the China Association for International Friendly Relations and its distribution will be overseen by AmeriCares representatives in China, the statement added.
Northwest, which operates seven weekly passenger flights to China, said it had received special permission for the relief flight to Shanghai.
The aircraft is one of eight 747 freighters Northwest operates in the Pacific region.
Northwest and AmeriCares teamed up in the past to help victims of the Kobe earthquake in January last year, when the airline flew more than 200 tonnes of relief supplies into Japan.
